transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Claire (Redwood AE), Miguel (Redwood SE), Janelle (Sundae Procurement), Tom (Sundae CISO), Ravi (Sundae ML), Sarah (Sundae Legal)

Summary: quick onboarding readiness workshop to align MSA/DPA redlines, SLA tiers, and keying/KMS approach for a pilot. Customer focused on data residency, KMS/HSM, SSO, billing path and committed usage. Redwood outlined hosting options (hosted API vs dedicated vs private VPC), fallback routing, and suggested pilot metrics.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA exceptions, KMS & HSM approach, SLA tiers & credits, pricing model (committed vs on-demand), pilot acceptance criteria, technical perf preflight.

Transcript:
[00:00] Claire Huang: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. Hi Janelle, hi Tom, hi Ravi, Sarah, Miguel from my side. We're here to walk through onboarding readiness — so legal, procurement and the SE bits together so nothing gets lost.
[00:28] Janelle Park: Thanks Claire, appreciate it. We wanted this session to make sure the redline path is clear and to understand any blockers for our procurement committee. We have a couple of nonstandard clauses, primarily around data residency and KMS.
[00:45] Miguel Santos: Cool, totally. Quick note — when we say KMS here we mean customer-managed keys in a cloud KMS or HSM; we also have an escrow/hybrid option for on-prem, there's a doc I'll link.
[01:10] Tom Breuer: We're concerned about tokenization of PII, egress, and audit logs — so the DPA has to reflect that we need audit-level events for model calls and key usage. Also, do you support bring-your-own-kms?
[01:30] Claire Huang: Yes, BYOK is supported for Private deployments and Dedicated in some regions. For hosted there are options too — customer-managed KMS with envelope encryption — Miguel can detail the tradeoffs.
[01:47] Miguel Santos: Right. For hosted API we can integrate with your cloud KMS for encrypting data at rest and keys for model artifacts; however full HSM-backed signing is only available on our Private and Dedicated+HSM plans. There's a small latency hit when doing remote HSM operations, we can quantify.
[02:15] Sarah Lee: Is that documented anywhere? We need specifics for legal (e.g., FIPS, HSM vendor, residency guarantees).
[02:27] Claire Huang: We'll include the KMS/HSM spec sheet in the redline packet. I'll add the FIPS/HSM vendor support matrix — Miguel, can you capture exact numbers?
[02:38] Miguel Santos: Yep, will add. Also, for pilot acceptance, we usually recommend a 48-hour throughput sanity run on a representative workload to validate tail latency and KV cache behavior — that was effective for several customers.
[02:55] Ravi Patel: That would be great. Our traces are bursty — lots of short chats and occasional long completions. We'll share token distribution. Expect spikes at EOD.
[03:10] Tom Breuer: And region-wise we need EU-only processing for specific datasets. Can Redwood pin compute to eu-west-1 for the pilot?
[03:24] Claire Huang: Yes, you can pin to region. For Hosted we have region routing, for Private it's entirely controlled by you. For Dedicated we can reserve capacity in a region. There may be slight price variations for region-specific capacity.
[03:42] Janelle Park: On pricing — procurement wants to know committed vs on-demand costs and what happens if we exceed committed usage. Also, any minimum term?
[03:56] Claire Huang: For Hosted API it's pay-as-you-go with no long-term commitment. For Dedicated we offer reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits. Exceeding committed usage can be charged at an overage rate; we can also enable burst capacity. We'll send an illustrative pricing sheet with examples.
[04:19] Miguel Santos: One thing to watch: aggressive batching and prefix caching reduce per-token cost but can change latency. If your SLAs target sub-100ms for short responses, we'll need a dedicated routing policy and likely dedicated capacity for the hot paths.
[04:40] Ravi Patel: Our SLOs are 100ms p95 for the assistant in production. Is that something Redwood can guarantee under SLA?
[04:50] Claire Huang: We have SLA tiers. For Dedicated we can commit to latency SLOs in the agreement and include credits. For Hosted, the SLA is more oriented to availability and soft latency guidance, not strict p95 latency guarantees unless you move to Dedicated/Private.
[05:10] Sarah Lee: On the MSA — we have a standard requirement for indemnities, liability caps and data handling for subprocessor lists. Can Redwood provide subprocessor details and an audited SOC2 report?
[05:26] Claire Huang: Yes — we provide SOC2 Type II reports; we'll share the latest. Subprocessor list is maintained and we'll add the major infra partners. For indemnities and caps, we can discuss, but standard commercial terms apply.
[05:41] Janelle Park: Any ability to add an addendum for our extended audit rights?
[05:46] Claire Huang: We can accept limited audit rights; full vendor audits are typically scoped under Private deployments. We'll note that as a redline item.
[05:56] Miguel Santos: Technical note — if you plan to keep logs for longer for compliance, Redwood can route logs to your log sink (SIEM) or deliver them via secure S3 with encryption. That avoids long-term storage on our hosted platform if that's a requirement.
[06:14] Tom Breuer: Good. We also want RBAC and SSO — SAML/SCIM integration for provisioning team access. How mature is that?
[06:24] Claire Huang: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning across all tiers. RBAC is configurable in the Console; roles can be mapped to SAML assertions. I'll include the docs link in the follow-up.
[06:36] Sarah Lee: For the DPA we've flagged two clauses: data substitution and cross-border transfer. We need clarity on subprocessors in APAC.
[06:47] Miguel Santos: We can show an AR (architecture) diagram that marks data flow and border crossing points. That usually helps legal with the clause. We'll include that.
[06:58] Janelle Park: Procurement question — what's typical onboarding timeline from signature to pilot? We have a fiscal window in March and need to be live before end of April.
[07:09] Claire Huang: Typical Hosted onboarding is a few days after paperwork cleared; for Dedicated it's more like 6–8 weeks depending on capacity and region. Private on-prem can take longer. For a pilot, if you go Hosted we can aim for 2–3 weeks from signed MSA+DPA; with Dedicated it depends on capacity lead time.
[07:29] Ravi Patel: We might start with hosted for the pilot to meet timeline and then transition to Dedicated. How much disruption is model/version pinning during that migration?
[07:39] Miguel Santos: We support consistent API and model versioning across environments. Migration is typically seamless if you pin a model version and use the same prompt and routing configs. You may need a short validation window for KV cache warming and latency tuning.
[07:55] Tom Breuer: About SLA credits — what's the mechanism for escalation? We need a committed contact and a runbook.
[08:03] Claire Huang: For Dedicated and Enterprise tiers we provide an on-call escalation ladder, dedicated CSM/Support contacts, and a runbook we can attach to the SLA. Minor outages are handled via standard support; severe incidents follow our incident response process with 24/7 pager escalation when included in the plan.
[08:22] Sarah Lee: Can we get a copy of that runbook to review?
[08:25] Claire Huang: Yes — will include in the follow-up packet.
[08:29] Miguel Santos: Quick perf question for Ravi — can you share token-size histograms (p50/p95 token lengths) and rough QPS expected for the pilot? That will let us size a Dedicated pool if you choose to.
[08:40] Ravi Patel: We'll share an export — expect average 40 tokens p50 and p95 around 400 tokens for long tasks; QPS during business hours maybe 8–12, spikes up to 50 for batch inference.
[08:55] Miguel Santos: Good, that helps. Also please share any model families you plan to use — open Llama variant vs proprietary, that affects quantization choices.
[09:06] Ravi Patel: We'll likely start with an open model, then test a finetuned variant.
[09:12] Janelle Park: On pricing again — can you show an example with two scenarios: 1) Hosted pilot 5k requests/day, 2) Dedicated reserve for 1 GPU-equivalent with burst? We need that for our FinOps review.
[09:28] Claire Huang: Absolutely — I'll attach a modeled pricing spreadsheet with both scenarios and per-token and per-hour breakdowns. Also show cost impact of caching and token-limits.
[09:43] Tom Breuer: One more item: we need explicit egress fee treatment — if data leaves EU, is there a transfer fee?
[09:51] Claire Huang: There are no vendor-level egress fees for host-to-host inside our platform, but cloud provider egress costs may apply if you move data across regions or external sinks. We'll call out any potential charges in the pricing sheet.
[10:08] Sarah Lee: For MSA redlines, we'll send you a prioritized list. We generally color-code must-haves vs negotiables.
[10:17] Claire Huang: Great — that'll speed review. We prefer one consolidated redline.
[10:22] Miguel Santos: Technical follow-up offer — we can run a short preflight benchmark with your traces to validate latency percentiles and recommend a quantization profile, batching config and KV cache settings. That will produce a small report (latency, p95, p99, token cost estimates).
[10:39] Ravi Patel: That perf report would be super helpful for our SREs.
[10:44] Claire Huang: Okay, to recap — action items: Claire sends redline + pricing sheet + SOC2 + runbook; Miguel runs 48-hour perf sanity; Ravi and team provide traces and region constraints; Sarah/Janelle to return prioritized redlines. We'll aim to reconvene after the perf run.
[11:08] Janelle Park: Sounds good. One ask — can we get an estimate for credit amounts for SLA breaches? Our procurement needs the numbers to model liability.
[11:15] Claire Huang: We'll include typical SLA credit tables for Dedicated tiers; for Hosted we provide availability credit tiers. We'll make sure numbers are explicit.
[11:26] Tom Breuer: Also please include what telemetry is exposed — request ids, timestamps, and per-token breakdown?
[11:32] Miguel Santos: We can surface request-level traces and token-level cost breakdown in the Console and via export. For PII reasons, we can redact payloads and only export telemetry.
[11:45] Sarah Lee: Thanks, that helps.
[11:48] Claire Huang: Any final questions?
[11:51] Ravi Patel: None from me. We'll start prepping traces.
[11:54] Janelle Park: No more, thanks.
[11:56] Claire Huang: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet and calendar invite for the perf readout on 2025-02-24.

End of transcript.

Referenced docs/links: Redwood MSA + DPA redline (to be shared), KMS/HSM spec sheet, SOC2 Type II (link to secure portal), pricing spreadsheet (link), perf run instructions (link).

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription glitches (e.g., KMS spelled K M S, HSM as H-S-M, and Redwood referenced sometimes as "Redwood Inference" and sometimes as "Redwood"), speaker overlaps and shorthand.
